# Tool reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_tool_docs.py from the server's own schemas. Do not edit by hand. -->

The server exposes 19 tools, 1 resource template and 1 prompt. Return types are the Pydantic models in [`models.py`](../src/merge_mcp/models.py).

## Discovery

### `find_issues_in_dependencies`

Find available issues in the libraries the user already depends on. Read the user's dependency files and pass them in; the server maps each package to its GitHub repository and searches those repos for newcomer-friendly issues, ranked by viability. People succeed more often on libraries they already use.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `manifests` | object[] \| null | no | Dependency files from the user's own projects, each as {'filename': 'package.json', 'content': '<file text>'}. Recognised names include requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, package.json, go.mod, Cargo.toml. |
| `packages` | object[] \| null | no | Or name packages directly, each as {'ecosystem': 'python', 'name': 'httpx'}. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum candidates. Default: `10`. |

Returns: `DependencyIssueResult` · read-only, calls GitHub

### `find_issues`

Search GitHub for open, unassigned issues with no linked pull request, ranked by a viability score that explains every deduction. Use assess_issue for a deeper check of one issue before starting work.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `language` | string \| null | no | Primary repo language, e.g. 'go'. Omit for any. |
| `labels` | string[] \| null | no | Issue labels that must all be present. Defaults to ['good first issue']. |
| `keywords` | string \| null | no | Free-text terms, e.g. a library or topic. |
| `repo` | string \| null | no | Limit to one repo, 'owner/name'. |
| `min_stars` | integer \| null | no | Skip repos with fewer stars. Default: `50`. |
| `updated_within_days` | integer \| null | no | Only issues with activity this recently. Default: `90`. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum candidates. Default: `10`. |

Returns: `IssueSearchResult` · read-only, calls GitHub

### `assess_issue`

Check whether one issue is worth starting: is it open, unassigned, unclaimed, free of competing pull requests, and in a repo that merges outside contributions? Returns the issue text plus a 0-100 score with reasons.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issue_url` | string | yes | https://github.com/owner/name/issues/N |

Returns: `IssueAssessment` · read-only, calls GitHub

## Workspace

### `start_workspace`

Clone a repository into a fresh workspace on a new branch and build its playbook (how to build and test it, conventions, contribution policy). Runs in the background: poll get_job with the returned job_id. The job result holds `workspace` and `playbook`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string \| null | no | 'owner/name' or a github.com URL. |
| `issue_url` | string \| null | no | Issue to work on. Implies the repo. |
| `ref` | string \| null | no | Branch, tag or commit. Defaults to the default branch. |
| `install_command` | string \| null | no | Override the detected dependency install command. |
| `test_command` | string \| null | no | Override the detected test command. |
| `use_ci` | boolean | no | Read install/test/lint commands from the repo's CI workflow. Set false to use the language's default commands instead. Default: `True`. |

Returns: `JobHandle` · calls GitHub

### `get_job`

Poll a background job. Returns state 'running', 'succeeded' (with `result`) or 'failed' (with `error`). Call again while it is running.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `job_id` | string | yes | Handle returned by a start_* tool. |
| `wait_seconds` | number | no | Wait up to this long for the job to finish. Default: `20`. |

Returns: `JobStatus` · read-only

### `get_playbook`

The repo's conventions: how to install, test and lint it (read from its CI), commit and pull request style, what past merged changes contained, and contribution policy (DCO, CLA, AI rules). Read it before editing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | Handle returned by start_workspace (ws_...). |

Returns: `Playbook` · read-only

### `find_precedents`

Show recent commits that changed the same files, with everything else each one touched (tests, changelog, docs). Use them as worked examples of how this project makes this kind of change.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | Handle returned by start_workspace (ws_...). |
| `paths` | string[] | yes | Files or directories you expect to change. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum commits. Default: `5`. |

Returns: `PrecedentList` · read-only

### `list_workspaces`

List workspaces on this machine, with the state of any linked pull request.

No parameters.

Returns: `list[Workspace]` · read-only

### `delete_workspace`

Delete a workspace and its checkout from disk. Uncommitted work is lost.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | Handle returned by start_workspace (ws_...). |

Returns: `str` · destructive

## Files

### `list_files`

List files in the workspace (tracked and new, ignoring .gitignore'd paths).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | Handle returned by start_workspace (ws_...). |
| `prefix` | string | no | Only paths under this directory. Default: ``. |

Returns: `FileList` · read-only

### `read_file`

Read a text file from the workspace, optionally a line range.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | Handle returned by start_workspace (ws_...). |
| `path` | string | yes | Path relative to the repository root. |
| `start_line` | integer | no | First line, 1-based. Default: `1`. |
| `max_lines` | integer | no | Lines to return. Default: `400`. |

Returns: `FileContent` · read-only

### `search_code`

Search file contents in the workspace. Returns path, line number and line text.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | Handle returned by start_workspace (ws_...). |
| `pattern` | string | yes | Extended regular expression (git grep -E). |
| `path_prefix` | string | no | Limit to this file or directory. Default: ``. |

Returns: `SearchResult` · read-only

### `edit_file`

Replace one exact occurrence of old_text in a file. Fails if it matches zero or several times, so include enough surrounding lines to be unique.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | Handle returned by start_workspace (ws_...). |
| `path` | string | yes | Path relative to the repository root. |
| `old_text` | string | yes | Exact text to replace. Must occur once. |
| `new_text` | string | yes | Replacement text. |

Returns: `WriteResult`

### `write_file`

Create or overwrite a file in the workspace. Prefer edit_file for small changes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | Handle returned by start_workspace (ws_...). |
| `path` | string | yes | Path relative to the repository root. |
| `content` | string | yes | Full new contents of the file. |

Returns: `WriteResult`

### `get_diff`

Show everything changed in the workspace since the base commit.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | Handle returned by start_workspace (ws_...). |

Returns: `DiffResult` · read-only

## Checks

### `start_check`

Run the repo's own setup, tests or linter in an isolated sandbox, using the commands from the playbook. Runs in the background: poll get_job. The result reports pass/fail, the end of the output and, where the test runner is understood, per-test outcomes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | Handle returned by start_workspace (ws_...). |
| `kind` | `setup` \| `test` \| `lint` | yes | 'setup' installs dependencies (run once, first). 'test' runs the repo's test suite. 'lint' runs its linter. |
| `test_ids` | string[] \| null | no | For kind='test', when the playbook says accepts_test_ids: files or test ids to run, e.g. ['tests/test_x.py::test_y']. Omit to run everything. |

Returns: `JobHandle`

### `check_readiness`

Pre-flight the current diff: have tests and the linter passed on it, and does it contain what this repo's merged changes usually contain (tests, a changelog entry)? Returns the findings a reviewer would likely raise. Fix them before prepare_pull_request.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | Handle returned by start_workspace (ws_...). |

Returns: `Readiness` · read-only

## Handoff and follow-up

### `prepare_pull_request`

Final step. Builds a pull request draft (title, body, checklist) and the commands the human must run to commit, push and open it. Nothing is submitted: show the checklist and commands to the user and stop.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | Handle returned by start_workspace (ws_...). |
| `title` | string | yes | Pull request title in the repo's style. |
| `summary` | string | yes | What changed and why, for the maintainer. |
| `testing_notes` | string | no | How the change was verified. Default: ``. |

Returns: `PullRequestDraft`

### `check_pull_request`

After the human has opened the pull request: read its CI results and reviews and return what to do next to get it merged. It only reads from GitHub; it never comments or pushes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pull_request_url` | string | yes | https://github.com/owner/name/pull/N |
| `workspace_id` | string \| null | no | Optional. Links the pull request to its workspace so list_workspaces shows its state. |

Returns: `PullRequestStatus` · calls GitHub

## Resources

- `mergemcp://workspaces/{workspace_id}/playbook`: The cached playbook for a workspace, as JSON.

## Prompts

- `contribute(issue_url)`: Guided workflow for contributing a fix for one GitHub issue.
